rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.5 and 3.1-3.5 report the authors' own two-season sorghum experiment (Samsun, Turkey, 2020-2021) with 68 UAV missions, water-bath calibration, 580 ground thermal measurements, machine-learning calibration and correlation of surface temperature with LAI, crop height and soil moisture (Tables 3-5, Figs. 3-7).
rows.notes: The study reports only the accuracy of UAV thermal sensors (RMSE reduced to ~1.3-1.4 C after XGBoost calibration), the effect of flight altitude, that georeferenced thermal orthomosaics distinguish soil/canopy and irrigation treatments (S1 coolest), and negative correlations of temperature with LAI, height and soil moisture. It does not report any result on irrigation planning, water use efficiency or water savings; these are mentioned only as potential applications in the introduction and conclusion. The study supports a precondition (accurate, spatially explicit thermal monitoring) of the claimed water-conservation effect, not the effect itself.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.5 and 3.1-3.5 report the authors' own field and laboratory experiment on sorghum under four drip irrigation treatments with UAV thermal sensors (Micasense Altum, FDP-R) validated against a Testo 875-i ground imager; results in Tables 3-5 and Figs. 3-7.
rows.notes: No yield, productivity or crop-production outcome is measured or reported; the study only shows that calibrated thermal orthomosaics correlate with phenotypic traits (LAI r = -0.66/-0.70, crop height r = -0.78/-0.69, soil moisture r = -0.59/-0.53) and capture treatment temperature differences. This is a precondition for site-specific management, not evidence that remote sensing delivers productivity gains.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a sensor-calibration/accuracy paper; it provides evidence that UAV thermal orthomosaics can be georeferenced and accurately monitor canopy temperature, but it does not test or report any effect on irrigation planning, water use efficiency or productivity. Both claim rows are therefore upstream.
